verdict.rationale: Sprinto documents user-built ingestion workflows, which its AI Editor can create from natural-language prompts and which webhooks trigger automatically. It also claims continuous monitoring, automated evidence collection and configurable AI risk auto-scoring, so some automation runs in the background without manual action. What the evidence shows is event-triggered and built-in monitoring rather than user-defined recurring schedules or autonomous agent runs, and the depth is thinly documented. Missing for 10: user-configurable recurring schedules or triggers beyond webhooks, documented autonomous multi-step agent execution, run history or observability for user automations, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Sprinto’s AI Editor helps you create and modify ingestion workflows using natural language prompts.
You can use webhooks to: Receive incoming payloads, Trigger ingestion workflows, Process external events
Audit readiness by design: Maintain readiness with continuous monitoring, alerts, and evidence collection.
You can configure: AI risk auto-scoring, Risk thresholds and scoring levels
